'''Ferland Sinna Mendy''' (born 8 June 1995) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] for {{Spanish football updater|Real Madrid}} club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].

Mendy began his senior career with [[Le Havre AC|Le Havre]] before joining [[Ligue 1]] side [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in 2017. He signed for Real Madrid in 2019, where he became a regular left-back and won multiple domestic and European honours, including three La Liga championships and two [[UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions Leagues]].

Mendy made his senior debut for [[France national football team|France]] in November 2018 and later represented the nation at [[UEFA Euro 2024]].

==Early life==
Mendy was born in [[Meulan-en-Yvelines]],<ref name=Soccerway/> and grew up in [[Ecquevilly]], in the western suburbs of Paris.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 August 2018 |title=Yvelines. Ecquevilly : Ils sont tous fiers de Ferland Mendy ! |url=https://actu.fr/ile-de-france/ecquevilly_78206/yvelines-ecquevilly-sont-tous-fiers-ferland-mendy_18331578.html |access-date=8 January 2024 |website=actu.fr |language=fr}}</ref> He is of Senegalese and Bissau-Guinean descent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.afrik-foot.com/senegal-aliou-cisse-met-la-pression-sur-ferland-mendy |title=Sénégal: Aliou Cissé met la pression sur Ferland Mendy |trans-title=Senegal: Aliou Cissé puts pressure on Ferland Mendy |website=Afrik-Foot |date=14 April 2018 |access-date=4 June 2019 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jeuneafrique.com/mag/468769/societe/football-le-senegal-reve-de-ferland-mendy/|title=Football : le Sénégal rêve de Ferland Mendy – Jeune Afrique|website=JeuneAfrique.com}}</ref> He acquired [[French nationality law|French nationality]] on 16 January 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JORF n° 0015 du 18 janvier 2007 – Légifrance |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/jo/id/JORFCONT000000001930 |access-date=1 January 2024 |website=legifrance.gouv.fr |page=1102 |language=fr |format=PDF}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
During the [[2016–17 Ligue 2]] season, Mendy made 35 appearances for [[Le Havre AC|Le Havre]].<ref name=lequipe>{{cite news |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Lyon-a-presente-ferland-mendy/814464 |title=Lyon a présenté Ferland Mendy |trans-title=Lyon introduced Ferland Mendy |newspaper=L'Équipe |date=29 June 2017 |access-date=4 June 2019 |language=fr}}</ref>
===Lyon===
[[File:Ferland Mendy 2017 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Mendy training with [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in 2017|285x285px]]
Mendy signed for [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on 29 June 2017 on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-za/news/lyon-ligue-1-transfer-news-ferland-mendy-rachid-ghezzal/89s8b0wzrchx158we4a796zm9 |title=Lyon sign Mendy but Ghezzal and Gonalons to depart |first=Jamie |last=Smith |website=Goal.com |publisher=Perform Group |date=29 June 2017 |access-date=4 June 2019}}</ref> The transfer fee paid to Le Havre was reported as €5&nbsp;million plus a possible €1&nbsp;million in bonuses.<ref name=lequipe/> On 19 September 2018, he made his [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut in a 2–1 away win over [[Manchester City]] in the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|2018–19]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2025064--man-city-vs-lyon/ |title=Man. City 1–2 Lyon |website=UEFA |date=19 September 2018 }}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
On 12 June 2019, Mendy signed for [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid]] on a six-year contract for an initial fee of €48&nbsp;million, potentially rising to €53&nbsp;million with add-ons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/06/official-announcement-mendy |title=Official Announcement: Mendy |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=12 June 2019 |access-date=12 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/articles/2019/06/12/ferland-mendy-completes-move-real-madrid |title=Ferland Mendy completes move to Real Madrid |publisher=Olympique Lyonnais |date=12 June 2019 |access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> He made his debut on 1 September 2019, starting in a 2–2 draw at [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/cronica/2019/09/01/5d6c32dc268e3ebc6b8b4569.html|title=Bale rescues a draw for Real Madrid|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=1 September 2019|access-date=1 September 2019}}</ref> His first goal came on 13 July 2020, in a 2–1 victory over [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid/story/4136211/mendy-scores-first-real-madrid-goal-with-exceptional-finish-in-8-10-display-as-los-blancos-top-granada|title=Mendy scores first Real Madrid goal with exceptional finish in 8/10 display as Los Blancos top Granada|date=14 July 2020|access-date=14 July 2020|website=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref> During the league season he appeared in 25 matches, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca}}</ref>

On 24 February 2021, he scored his first Champions League goal in a 1–0 away win over [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] in the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|2020–21]] season round of 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/feb/24/atalanta-v-real-madrid-champions-league-last-16-live |title=Atalanta v Real Madrid: Champions League last 16 – as it happened |website=The Guardian |date=24 February 2021 }}</ref> In the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|2021–22 Champions League]] semi-final second leg, he made a goal-line clearance to prevent [[Manchester City]]'s [[Jack Grealish]] from scoring in the 87th minute and keep the score at 0–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.givemesport.com/88003608-real-madrid-3-1-man-city-ferland-mendys-insane-87th-minute-clearance/ |title=Real Madrid 3–1 Man City: Ferland Mendy's insane 87th minute clearance |publisher=GiveMeSport |date=5 May 2022 }}</ref> However, Real Madrid managed to turn the tie by late goals and extra-time to win 3–1 (6–5 on aggregate) and reach the [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2022/may/04/real-madrid-v-manchester-city-champions-league-semi-final-second-leg-live |title=Real Madrid 3–1 Man City |work=The Guardian |date=4 May 2022 }}</ref>

==International career==
In November 2018, Mendy was called up for the [[France national football team|France national team]] for the first time after the injury-enforced withdrawal of [[Benjamin Mendy]] for the matches against [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]] and [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]]. He made his debut against the latter playing all 90 minutes of a 1–0 home win.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/11/20/world-champion-france-beats-uruguay-to-cap-successful-year/38575605/ |title=World champion France beats Uruguay to cap successful year |newspaper=USA Today |date=20 November 2018 |access-date=4 June 2019}}</ref>

On 16 May 2024, Mendy was selected for France to participate in the [[UEFA Euro 2024]]. He did not play any matches.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2024 |title=Les vingt-cinq Bleus pour l'Euro |url=https://www.fff.fr/article/12507-les-vingt-cinq-bleus-pour-l-euro.html |access-date=16 May 2024 |publisher=[[Fédération Française de Football]] |language=fr}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mendy is a cousin of goalkeeper [[Édouard Mendy]], who plays for [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] and the [[Senegal national football team|Senegal national team]].<ref>{{cite web |date=31 August 2020 |title=Édouard Mendy: 5 things on the Rennes and Senegal goalkeeper |url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/NEWS/2020/08/31/edouard-mendy-5-things-on-the-rennes-and-senegal-goalkeeper |access-date=17 April 2021 |publisher=Ligue 1}}</ref>

At the age of 15, Mendy spent time in a wheelchair after hip surgery and was told he might never play football again.<ref>{{cite news |date=19 June 2019 |title=Ferland Mendy: 'I was in a wheelchair, now I'm at Real Madrid' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48699502 |access-date=2 July 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Mendy is a Muslim.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ukpai |first=Kingsley |date=28 February 2025 |title=Which Real Madrid players will be fasting during this Ramadan |url=https://tribuna.com/en/blogs/which-real-madrid-players-will-be-fasting-during-this-ramada/ |access-date=30 October 2025 |website=Tribuna.com}}</ref>
